title: add nvtx ranges, counters, microbench instrumentation and perf dashboard
author: Asha Patel
description: Motivation: Better visibility into runtime hot paths has been a recurring blocker for both kernel optimization and scheduling work. This PR adds NVTX ranges and lightweight counters around key serving runtime components (scheduler, KV cache hits/loads, continuous batching boundaries, kernel dispatch) plus a microbench harness and Grafana dashboard to make the signals consumable by SRE and perf engineers. The change is intentionally conservative: NVTX ranges are opt-in at runtime via config flags and have no effect on logic paths when disabled. We also add a small microbenchmark binary (microbench/runtime_microbench) that exercises request batching and KV cache behavior with configurable sequence lengths to generate reproducible profiles. Summary of changes: - runtime/trace: add NVTXRange scoped helpers and enum tags for Scheduler, KernelDispatch, KVCache, ContinuousBatching, TokenDecode. NVTX is gated by build-time flag and runtime env REDWOOD_NVTX=1. - runtime/metrics: add atomic counters for kv_cache_hits, kv_cache_misses, batches_created, batch_flushes, kernel_invocations and exposed via existing Prometheus endpoint. - runtime/scheduler: instrument schedule and flush boundaries with NVTX ranges and increment counters at key transitions. Add light-weight timing histograms for batch wait times. - runtime/kv_cache: increment counters on hit/miss paths; add optional sample key tagging for NVTX ranges. - perf/microbench: new microbench harness with command-line knobs for concurrency, seq-len distribution, batch size target, and kernel sim mode. Produces CSVs and can emit Prometheus pushgateway metrics for CI. - observability/dashboards: add grafana/dashboard runtime-perf-nvtx.json that maps counters and example NVTX trace screenshots with recommended alert thresholds. - docs: updated README for microbench and how-to enable NVTX and collect traces (NVIDIA Nsight, perf). Testing: Local microbench runs and CI unit tests for metric exports. Ran microbench against two GPUs (A100, 4090) and an emulated CPU path to validate metrics. No functional API changes, feature is opt-in and covered by unit tests for the metrics plumbing. Related: ENG-2145 (profiling baseline), ENG-2198 (scheduler improvements).

review_comments: Evan Brooks: Can we ensure NVTX no-ops completely when REDWOOD_NVTX is unset? I want zero perf delta in production defaults.
Marina Chen: Dashboard looks good; suggest adding a panel that correlates batch_wait_p95 with kernel_invocations to help diagnose oversubscription.
Dmitri Volkov: Microbench is great, but please add a CI job that runs the microbench in sim mode to catch regressions in scheduling logic.
Evan Brooks: Use clear metric names (redwood_runtime_kv_cache_hits vs kv_cache_hits) so Prom queries are unambiguous across services.
author_responses: Author: NVTX helper is compiled out when REDWOOD_NVTX=0 and the runtime check returns early. Verified with local perf runs; added unit smoke test asserting no NVTX symbols in the binary when disabled.
Author: Added a grafana panel correlating batch_wait_p95 and kernel_invocations and documented the PromQL used.
Author: Added a lightweight CI job (microbench-sim) that runs the harness in kernel-sim mode for linux-x86 to the perf CI matrix (non-blocking).
Author: Prefixed runtime metrics with redwood_runtime_ to avoid collisions; updated registry and tests accordingly.
